claim: the float64 reference is now as validated as it can be made, on five independent axes, and every remaining gap in this campaign is therefore OURS.

axis_1_independent_rebuild_is_BIT_IDENTI.what: the finite-difference run rebuilt the reference from scratch in its own process, hours after the frozen bundle was built
axis_1_independent_rebuild_is_BIT_IDENTI.why_it_matters: this is the A/A arm the campaign never had. Two independent builds, one sha256. The reference's own reproducibility floor is EXACTLY ZERO, not "small".

axis_2_finite_differences.coverage_statement: 5 of 8 in diffusion_module, which holds 89.211 % of the gradient mass; one each in pairformer_stack, aux_heads and msa_module -- every section above 1 % of the squared norm got at least one. Under the retired uniform-over-tensors draw diffusion had a 19.9 % chance of ZERO samples and pairformer, with 65.6 % of the tensor COUNT, would have taken most of eight.
axis_2_finite_differences.note: two samples land in diffusion_conditioning -- the sub-module holding 33.61 % of the diffusion magnitude that sits outside our DiffusionModule boundary -- and two land on attention_pair_bias / conditioned_transition layer norms, the family that owns the error tail. Both validate: 5.088e-03 and 1.501e-05, 8.411e-06 and 9.515e-05.

mass_coverage_pass151.why_this_is_stated: this axis was reported by COUNT (8 of 4,170) and by SECTION (4 sections hit). Both understate it. By mass the set validates 22.9369 % of the gradient, and it happens to include the #2 and #3 heaviest tensors in the whole model. Count-based coverage of a mass-concentrated gradient is the wrong denominator in both directions -- it made this look weaker than it is, and it would make a uniform sample look stronger than it is.
mass_coverage_pass151.the_caveat_that_goes_with_it: the set's WORST agreement, rel 5.088e-03, is on diffusion_conditioning.transition_s.1.layer_norm.bias -- the #2 heaviest tensor in the model. The reference's own finite-difference validation is loosest exactly where the mass peaks. It is still ~10x inside the 5.0e-02 per-tensor bar, so nothing here is disqualified, but any claim resting on this axis should quote 5.088e-03 with the tensor it belongs to rather than the 5.508e-05 median.
mass_coverage_pass151.not_covered: the #1 and #4 heaviest tensors (transition_s.0.layer_norm.bias at 10.38237 % and diffusion_transformer.blocks.8.attention_pair_bias.layer_norm_a.layer_norm_s.weight at 8.05416 %) were NOT finite-difference validated. Extending the FD set to those two would take direct coverage past 41 %.

axis_3_revision: D22/D23: built at 0.4.3, the revision the checkpoint belongs to, missing=1 (version_tensor) / unexpected=0, upstream's own loader accepts it
axis_4_replay: 45/45 torch.randn draws and 2/2 python random draws replayed, 0 mismatches, loss bit-identical on replay
axis_5_boundary_capture: capture_vs_bundle worst_rel 0.0 at every one of the 7 ladder boundaries
what_this_licenses: D22/D23 controlled the reference's REVISION. Axis 2 controls its NUMERICAL CORRECTNESS. Axis 1 controls its REPRODUCIBILITY, exactly. So when the device gradient reads 1.6588e-01 at model scope, or 1.0575 on the one tensor FD validated to 3.990e-03, the disagreement is not the reference's. Every remaining gap is ours.
what_it_does_NOT_license: FD validates the reference, not our port. It cannot say WHICH of our stages is wrong -- only that the thing we are measured against is right. And 8 samples is 8 of 4,170 parameters: the coverage claim is "every section above 1 % of the squared norm was hit", not "every tensor was checked".
